transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-22
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Ellen Park (CTO, RidgePoint), Marcus Lee (AI Platform), Sofia Chen (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
RidgePoint is consolidating multiple inference vendors (OpenAI + in-house vLLM + Azure endpoints) into a single runtime. Primary drivers: cost reduction, consistent latency, security posture for a pharma client subsidiary that requires air-gapped options. They are evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private Redwood options and need eval parity with current TGI/vLLM runtimes. Next steps: security docs, pricing, benchmark plan.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya: Hey thanks everyone for making time, uh this is Maya from Redwood, AE on the account, with Diego who's our SE. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Ellen: Good, hi Maya, hi Diego, thanks. Ellen here. we've got about forty five minutes. Marcus and Sofia are on the line too.
[00:12] Marcus: hey all.
[00:13] Sofia: hi.
[00:15] Diego: great, quick agenda, I want to understand current stack and pain points, then deep dive on hosting tradeoffs and what a pilot could look like.
[00:22] Ellen: perfect. high level from RidgePoint — we've been running a mixed stack. we use OpenAI for a lot of chat features, we have an internal fleet running vLLM for some lower-level services, and a handful of models on AzureML for larger-batch inference. It's fragmented and costs are spiky, esp during peak reports. main asks: predictable cost, matching our latency SLOs (~120ms p50 for short prompts), and data controls for healthcare dataset — our pharma partner needs stronger isolation.
[00:40] Maya: ok that's helpful. when you say vLLM internal fleet, is that on-prem or cloud?
[00:44] Marcus: mixed — some on prem, some in our GCP project. we've also been trialing TGI on a few nodes, that's the 'tee-gee-eye' stack.
[00:50] Diego: cool. two immediate questions: what does success look like for you in the first 90 days? and what are the blockers for moving off OpenAI or consolidating?
[00:58] Ellen: success = ability to route most production traffic to a single provider without feature regressions. blockers: compliance sign-off (SOC2 + ISO), SSO integration, and the eval parity — API outputs must match or be within acceptable delta for our prompt set. also cost per token must not increase.
[01:12] Maya: makes sense. on parity — we usually do side-by-side evals with the same prompts, compare generation score and hallucination metrics. we'll share a sample eval harness. is Marcus the owner of that prompt set?
[01:22] Marcus: yup, I can share. it's about 120 canonical prompts and a smaller subset of 12 high-sensitivity prompts for the pharma flows.
[01:30] Sofia: quick security note — the pharma subsidiary requires either Private (VPC on customer side) or an on-prem package that can be air-gapped for audits. Hosted won't cut it for those datasets unless you can attest to dedicated tenancy and KMS controls.
[01:44] Diego: understood. Redwood Private supports customer VPC with a private control plane and can integrate with customer KMS/HSM. For on-prem airgapped, we have an on-prem package but timeline and support are heavier.
[01:55] Ellen: timeline's important — their compliance board wants a plan by end of Q3.
[01:59] Maya: okay, that's 2026-09-30 target. for timeline we normally do a proof of concept: pilot on Hosted with a dedicated pool or Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity to validate latency and cost, then move to Private if compliance requires. would you be open to a staged approach?
[02:13] Ellen: yes, staged is preferable. we want to see measurable unit economics and a rollback plan.
[02:18] Marcus: curious about performance — our v-l-l-m fleet is tuned for low-latency by doing aggressive KV caching and custom batching. can Redwood replicate those patterns?
[02:27] Diego: yes, runtime supports prefix and KV cache and workload-aware batching. in dedicated pools we can pin GPU families and select kernels per model. one thing to note: quantization can change output slightly; if you need bit-exact outputs we avoid aggressive 4-bit for the sensitive flows.
[02:42] Marcus: any hard numbers you can share for 70B class models on Dedicated? p50 and p95?
[02:47] Diego: broadly, on an A10G-like profile we see p50 ~90-120ms for 512-token short calls with continuous batching tuned; p95 ~250-300ms depending on burst. but these numbers are workload dependent — we'll run your prompts to get real numbers.
[03:02] Ellen: that's promising. cost tradeoffs? we care about cost per generated token and also token input cost since we do a lot of structured parsing.
[03:11] Maya: Redwood Optimize gives batching/caching suggestions and model/quantization recommendations per workload. for cost we can show scenarios: Hosted pay-as-you-go, Dedicated reserved capacity with baseline commit, and Private licensing + infra. Typical customers see 20-45% lower unit cost after tuning caching and batching.
[03:26] Sofia: about logs and audit trails — we need audit logs for each token request, redaction controls, and retention settings. any limitations?
[03:34] Diego: we provide per-token tracing and per-route dashboards, with configurable retention. for Private we can ship logs to your SIEM or keep them in your KMS-backed storage.
[03:43] Sofia: nice. and SSO / RBAC?
[03:46] Maya: SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access controls are supported. Enterprise customers use fine-grained RBAC with key rotation via KMS.
[03:55] Marcus: what about fallback and graceful degradation? we sometimes need to overflow to a cheaper model during spikes.
[04:00] Diego: smart routing policies allow routing by latency, cost, and region. you can configure fallback to smaller model families or other regions; we also have automatic model variants for capacity constrained events.
[04:10] Ellen: how invasive is the integration? will we need to refactor call shapes?
[04:14] Maya: Redwood aims for minimal changes: same REST/SDK patterns. we support function-calling, streaming and structured outputs. potentially the only changes are model selection and any socket/prefix caching hooks if you want advanced KV cache integration.
[04:27] Marcus: one technical smell from our side — we've integrated KV cache in application layer with LRU logic. would you recommend moving that into Redwood caching?
[04:35] Diego: prefix caching at the platform level reduces duplicate compute and simplifies your app. we can expose hooks so you can keep app-level controls while benefiting from platform cache.
[04:43] Sofia: any third-party penetration tests or compliance attestations we can pass to security?
[04:48] Maya: yeah we'll include SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001 cert, and our recent pen-test summary. for Dedicated and Private we can also provide architecture diagrams and runbook for audits.
[04:59] Ellen: great. one more thing — we'd like to run a head-to-head with TGI for our highest-volume endpoint. can we do that?
[05:05] Diego: absolutely. typical plan: we run your 12 sensitivity prompts and the 120 canonical prompts across your main models and variants, capture latency, cost, and quality metrics. we can run in Hosted Dedicated pool to start if you want the low-friction path.
[05:18] Marcus: sweet. about pricing for Dedicated — do you do short-term commits or only annual?
[05:23] Maya: we offer monthly and annual reserved capacity. monthly is more flexible but slightly higher unit cost; annual has deeper discounts. for pilots we often do a 1-month reserved at pilot rates.
[05:33] Sofia: compliance aside, what are the ops responsibilities during a pilot? who owns incident response?
[05:39] Diego: for Hosted and Dedicated Redwood handles runtime ops; we provide monitoring and on-call hooks. for Private on-prem, runbook responsibilities are shared — Redwood provides deployment support and a transfer of runbooks to your ops team.
[05:51] Ellen: ok. any major compatibility gotchas with our current model artifacts (we use a mix of HF-flavored checkpoints, some TRL fine-tuned artifacts, and TGI format)?
[06:00] Diego: we support common HF checkpoints and can load TGI artifacts in many cases, though there are sometimes tokenizer or generation-config differences. we do a compatibility pass during onboarding and flag any conversion steps.
[06:11] Marcus: tokenizer mismatches bite us often — will you preserve tokenization and special tokens?
[06:15] Diego: yes, we preserve tokenizer configs and can mount your tokenizer files in Private or handle conversion in Dedicated. we'll log any tokenization diffs in the eval.
[06:23] Ellen: great. any latency impact from encryption / KMS operations if we use customer-managed keys?
[06:28] Diego: minimal; KMS signing happens at handshake and key unwrap, runtime caching reduces per-request crypto overhead. we'll provide numbers in the benchmark.
[06:36] Maya: sounds like we have alignment. proposed pilot: 2-week functional parity run in Hosted Dedicated pool using your 120/12 prompt sets, then an optional 2-week performance run with dedicated reserved nodes. does that match your expectations and timeline for Q3 sign-off?
[06:50] Ellen: yes that seems doable. we need the security pack before committing.
[06:54] Sofia: and the pilot scope must include the air-gapped option evaluation steps for the pharma flows — even if the pilot runs Hosted initially, we need a path to Private.
[07:03] Maya: noted. we'll include Private transition steps in the runbook.
[07:07] Marcus: one last question — you mentioned quantization earlier, will you simulate the 4-bit footprint but keep a no-quantize branch for the sensitive prompts?
[07:16] Diego: exactly. we recommend model variants: a quantized cheaper variant for bulk traffic and a full-precision variant for sensitive flows. routing policy can be per-endpoint.
[07:25] Ellen: ok good.
[07:27] Maya: great. any other blockers?
[07:29] Sofia: just internal legal review on data residency — I'll add that to the checklist I'm sending.
[07:33] Marcus: nothing from me.
[07:34] Maya: cool, recap then next steps: we'll send the security pack (SOC2/ISO/pen-test), sample eval harness and benchmark plan, Hosted vs Dedicated pricing and a pilot proposal for 1-month reserved trial. Diego will prepare runbook and latency/cost spreadsheet. We schedule the benchmark for Aug 3-7 pending your sign-off.
[07:52] Ellen: thanks, that works.
[07:54] Maya: awesome, we'll follow up with calendar invites and materials. thanks everyone.
[07:58] Marcus: thanks.
[07:59] Sofia: thanks all.
[08:00] End of meeting
